Chance-constrained optimal dispatch of integrated energy systems based on
data-driven sparse polynomial chaos expansion✩
Bo Dong a, Peng Lia,∗, Hao Yua, Haoran Jia, Guanyu Songa, Juan Lib, Jinli Zhaoa,
Chengshan Wang a
a Key Laboratory of Smart Grid of Ministry of Education, Tianjin University, Tianjin 300072, China

A R T I C L E I N F O
Keywords:
Integrated energy system
Data-driven sparse polynomial chaos expansion
Chance constraints
Day-ahead optimal dispatch
A B S T R A C T
In integrated energy systems, stochastic variations of different energy types of loads and the increasing
penetration of renewable energy generation have resulted in considerable uncertainties. These uncertainties
pose significant challenges to the economics and safe operation of integrated energy systems. Conventional
deterministic methods of optimal dispatch overlook the effects of uncertainties, while stochastic optimization,
though accounting for uncertainties, often yields conservative solutions that may adversely affect the economic
operations. Chance-constrained optimization can effectively deal with uncertainties and provide more flexibility
in balancing operational risks and benefits by expanding the feasible region. Hence, this paper proposes a
chance-constrained optimal dispatch method for integrated energy systems and employs data-driven sparse
polynomial chaos expansion method to enhance solving efficiency. First, the proposed chance-constrained
optimization aims to ensure the optimal economic operation with an affordable security confidence level that
balances safety and economics compared with deterministic and stochastic optimizations. The introduced data-
driven sparse polynomial chaos expansion method enables the fast computing of the output response using
only historical data, i.e., without knowledge pertaining to the distribution functions. Moreover, an improved
iterative verification structure is proposed, which further improves the convergence speed and accuracy.
Finally, the advantages and feasibility of the proposed method are verified using a test case and compared
with those of deterministic and stochastic optimization. Results show that the proposed method successfully
reduces the operational cost and controls violation probability.
Introduction
The global energy crisis and environmental problems caused by
fossil fuels have prompted interest in clean, reliable, efficient, and
economical energy technologies and infrastructure. To coordinate the
construction and operation of energy systems, conventional separate
energy networks for gas, electricity, and heat are interconnected via
energy conversion equipment, thus forming integrated energy systems
(IESs). An IES integrates the generation, distribution, storage, and
utilization of diverse energy carriers, offering a versatile and effec-
tive energy provision for a wide range of consumer needs [ 1]. The
synergistic benefits of IESs are significant, such as enhancing energy
efficiency [2], facilitating the consumption of renewable resources [3],
improving energy supply reliability and resilience [4], and contributing
to environmental sustainability [ 5]. Therefore, IESs have been widely

gies obtained from deterministic optimization. For example, load and
renewable energy fluctuations in electricity networks may result in
voltage deviations [15] or power outages in the electrical equipment of
other energy networks [16]. A gas-fired combined power and heat plant
may require adjustment to its output to satisfy uncertain electricity
and heat demands, which consequently affects the operational status
of the gas network [17]. In these cases, deterministic optimization
methods, which rely on fixed and known input parameters, cannot
address complex uncertainties in IESs and may result in conservative,
sub-optimal, or even infeasible operation strategies [18].
Significant efforts have been dedicated to address uncertainties in
the dispatch of IESs, which can be classified into three categories:
stochastic optimization [19], robust optimization [20], and interval
optimization [21]. All of these methods have been widely utilized in
the operation optimization of electric and integrated energy systems.
Compared with stochastic optimization methods, robust and interval
optimization methods do not require exact probabilistic distribution
functions. Specifically, robust optimization methods address uncertain-
ties by optimizing the worst case within a specified uncertainty set,
whereas interval optimization methods require only the upper and
lower bounds of random variables. However, compared with stochastic
optimization, both robust and interval optimization methods are more
conservative. Employing detailed probabilistic distribution functions
that capture the characteristics of uncertain variables more precisely
enables stochastic optimization methods to achieve higher accuracy
and feasibility [22,23].
As a further developed stochastic optimization method, chance-
constrained optimization (CCO) explicitly considers uncertainties by
introducing probabilistic constraints, and further expands the feasible
region by allowing the state variables to violate the constraints with a

optimization aims to find solutions that are less conservative and
more in line with the specified risk levels [25]. Chance-constrained
optimization allows the conservativeness of the optimal strategies to be
adjusted, which provides better control over trade-offs between risk and
benefits [26]. This can lead to more cost-effective and realistic solutions
in practical applications.
The application of CCO to the optimal dispatch of IESs presents
two major challenges. First, chance constraints in an IES present strong
non-convexity and non-linearity because of the pipeline transmission
characteristics of energy networks. A solution to this issue, as in power
systems, is to transform chance constraints into closed-form determin-
istic or tractable problems that can be easily solved using linear or
nonlinear programming solvers [27,28]. This transformation relies on
deliberately designed modeling methods that are not applicable or are
difficult to derive for IESs with diverse configurations and structures.
Another solution involves using samples from chance constraints and
converting them into multiple deterministic constraints, as represented
by the Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) method [29]. However, sam-
pling methods are generally computationally expensive, particularly for
high-dimensional and complex IESs.
Second, as a type of stochastic optimization method, CCO requires
knowledge pertaining to the probability density functions (PDFs) of
random variables. However, various uncertainties arising from the
loads and distributed generation in IESs cannot be depicted easily using
exact probability distribution functions. Although some typical distribu-
tions can be adopted as approximations, such as the beta distribution
for photovoltaic generation, Weibull distribution for wind generation,
and uniform distribution for loads, these approximations may deviate
from the actual uncertainty properties and thus result in significant
errors. Moreover, complex correlations typically exist among uncertain
factors, which further complicates the derivation of accurate PDFs [30].
This study is performed to devise an accurate and efficient CCO-
based optimal dispatch method for electric–heat–gas IESs that considers
arbitrary uncertainties from distributed generation and loads. In our
previous study [31], we developed a probabilistic power-flow calcula-
tion method for IESs using sparse polynomial chaos expansion (SPCE),
which is advantageous in terms of calculation efficiency and accuracy.
In this study, the aforementioned method is further extended to account
for arbitrary uncertainties using the concept of data-driven sparse
polynomial chaos expansion (DDSPCE). The DDSPEC-based model is
integrated into a chance-constrained optimal dispatch model of an IES
to realize economic operation under uncertain scenarios with accept-
able risks. A schematic illustration of the proposed method is shown in
Fig. 1.
The main contributions of this study are summarized as follows:
(1) A probabilistic model of the IES operation state is developed
based on data-driven sparse polynomial chaos expansion. The PDFs of
the state variables of the IES can be efficiently obtained by considering
the uncertainties from the distributed generation and loads with arbi-
trary distribution properties. The proposed model achieves an accuracy
level similar to that of the Monte Carlo method, and the computational
burden is reduced significantly.
(2) A day-ahead optimal dispatch method for the IES is proposed
based on CCO. The probabilistic model of the IES is utilized to for-
mulate chance constraints and evaluate the violation probability. The
holistic CCO-based model is converted into a second-order
cone-programming model to enable an easier solution. An improved
iterative procedure is designed to ensure higher convergence precision.
(3) The day-ahead optimal dispatch of an electricity–gas–heat IES is
realized using the proposed method, which balances between economic
performance and operational safety. The conservation of the operation
strategy is reduced compared with robust optimization, whereas the
operational violation risk is controllable compared with conventional
deterministic optimal dispatch methods.

(3) Operation constraints of distributed generator (DG) and electric
storage (ES)
The operational constraints of DGs and ES are considered in this
study using the typical operation dispatch model [ 33].
In actual industrial applications, the operational constraints in an
IES can be classified into soft and hard constraints [ 27]. For soft con-
straints, such as voltage and current magnitude constraints, as shown

under- or over-voltage, or a transmission line overload. Generally, a
low violation probability of the soft constraints is acceptable in actual
applications. However, hard constraints such as storage and generation
constraints, are physically impossible to violate.
Therefore, because the operational constraints of DGs and ES are
hard constraints that do not contain chance constraints, the model
description of DGs and ES is introduced in Appendix ‘‘Operation con-

As the chance-constrained optimal dispatch model and the DDSPCE

Solving scheme of chance-constrained day-ahead optimal dispatch model
The proposed optimization model contains chance constraints that
cannot be addressed directly using deterministic optimization solvers.
In existing studies, one-shot [ 43] and iterative [ 44] methods are typi-
cally used to manage chance constraints. The one-shot method refor-
mulates chance constraints into deterministic constraints and solves
the problem directly, which is a more suitable structure for intrusive
methods (e.g. generalized polynomial chaos). Meanwhile, the iterative
method is typically used in non-intrusive methods such as the MCS.
The core idea of the iterative method is to solve the deterministic
problem without chance constraints multiple times while verifying the
satisfaction of chance constraints in each iteration and adjusting the
boundaries of the deterministic problem for the next iterative step.
When the iterations converge, the solution to the deterministic prob-
lem, which is also the solution to the chance-constrained problem, is
obtained.
In this study, the DDSPCE method was used in conjunction with an
iterative computational framework. Owing to its rapid computation of
probability density functions, DDSPCE can significantly facilitate the
verification speed of chance constraints and effectively solve chance-
constrained problems. The iterative solution framework for the chance-
constrained optimization problem based on DDSPCE is illustrated in

Case study
A test IES case was used to verify the feasibility and advantages of

The three subsystems are connected through four energy stations, the

Three scenarios were considered, as follows:
Scenario 1: The operation strategy is obtained through determin-

In summary, the advantages of chance-constrained optimization
compared to other methods are as follows:
(1) Chance-constrained optimization can effectively deal with the
uncertainties in IES, restrict the violation risk to a predefined con-
fidence level, and enhance the ability of the system to deal with
unexpected events and the impact of uncertainties. Compared with
deterministic optimization, the maximum violation risk decreased from
36% to 10%.
(2) Chance-constrained optimization can provide more flexibility in
balancing operational risks and benefits, avoiding overly conservative
operational strategies for preventing low probability extreme scenarios.
Compared with stochastic optimization, the chance-constrained opti-
mization under a confidence level of 90% can reduce the operation cost
by 4.39%.

Conclusion
A DDSPCE method for the chance-constrained optimal dispatch
of an IES was proposed herein. By adopting DDSPCE, numerous de-
pendent samples were efficiently evaluated to estimate the violation
probability for each chance constraint, and the accuracy was verified
via comparison with MCS. Moreover, the proposed improved iterative
structure for the verification of chance constraints effectively reduced
the number of iterative steps and increased the calculation speed. These
contributions allowed us to obtain a fast and accurate solution for the
chance-constrained optimal dispatch. Finally, the proposed method was
applied to a test case for an IES, and the obtained optimization strat-
egy was evaluated and compared using deterministic and stochastic
optimization strategies. The results showed that, compared with the
deterministic strategy, the proposed method effectively controlled the
violation probability to the preset confidence level, thus ensuring the
safe operation of the IES. Compared with the conservative stochastic
optimization method, the proposed method reduced the operational
cost by 4.39% at a confidence level of 90%. Selecting a lower con-
fidence level allows the operational cost to be further reduced while
ensuring operational safety.
However, this study only considered the steady-state model of the
IES; in actual applications, the transmission delay of gas and heat
